\subsection*{Class NP --- Exhaustive Replay: Results}

\begin{theorem}[Exhaustive Decider for Bounded Runs]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.exists_exhaustiveDecider}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.exists_exhaustiveDecider}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin}
For every finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ over the binary alphabet,
there are a finite deterministic Turing machine $E$ over that alphabet and a natural
number $C$ such that the following holds for every binary input $z$ and
$T\in\mathbb{N}$. If every branch of $N$ on $z$ has halted within $T$ steps, then $E$
computes the output $[1]$ within exactly $C2^{C(T+1)}$ steps when $N$ accepts $z$ within
$T$ steps, and computes $[0]$ within exactly that many steps when $N$ does not accept
$z$ within $T$ steps.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Deterministic decision from a universal simulator]
\lean{Turing.ndAcceptsWithin_decider_of_universal}
\label{Turing.ndAcceptsWithin_decider_of_universal}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.CodeNDTM.toFinNDTM, Turing.EffectiveNDMachineCode, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin, Turing.FinNDTM.exists_exhaustiveDecider, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
Let $c$ be an effective code for nondeterministic Boolean machines, and suppose there is
a finite-state nondeterministic Boolean machine $U_N$ such that for every Boolean string
$\alpha$ there is a natural number $C$ for which, on every Boolean input $x$ and time
bound $t$, every choice sequence of length exactly $C(t+1)$ makes $U_N$ halt on
$\langle\langle\mathrm{bits}(t),\alpha\rangle,x\rangle$. Suppose also that $U_N$ has an
accepting computation of exactly that length if and only if the machine decoded from
$\alpha$ has an accepting computation on $x$ using exactly $t$ choices. Then there is a
finite-state deterministic Boolean machine $B_F$ such that, for each $\alpha$, some
natural number $C$ works for every $x$ and $t$: if the decoded machine accepts $x$ using
exactly $t$ choices, $B_F$ computes output $[1]$ on the paired input at exactly
$C2^{C(t+1)}$ steps; if it does not, $B_F$ computes output $[0]$ on that input at
exactly the same time.
\end{theorem}
